_comment: Policy for .claude/hooks/guard-protected-orgs.cjs. Agents never deploy, validate, or run Apex or Flow tests against production. The guard blocks production orgs and orgs it cannot classify. It lets a change to a sandbox or scratch org pass with no question: the rule salesforce-org-safety.md says when the agent asks the owner first. The owner runs production changes.

_fields.action: deny = block commands against recognized production orgs; ask = confirm. This project uses deny. An Apex or Flow test run against production gets the same decision as a deploy.
_fields.unknownOrgAction: What to do when the target org can't be classified (not authenticated yet, sf CLI unavailable). Any value other than 'allow' treats the org like production and applies 'action'. 'allow' = let it through.
_fields.sandboxAction: What to do when a deploy, data write, anonymous Apex run, or metadata delete targets a sandbox or scratch org. 'allow' = let it through with no question. This project uses allow: the safety rule says when the agent asks the owner first, and the owner turns those questions off and on by telling the agent. 'ask' = the guard also confirms each one. A deploy validate or an Apex or Flow test run on a sandbox always passes with no question.
_fields.confirmOrgDeleteAlways: true = any 'org delete' asks even for scratch/sandbox, since it's irreversible. Set false to only guard production.
_fields.alwaysProtect: Org aliases or usernames to always confirm, even if auto-detected as sandbox/scratch. Example: ["target-build"].
_fields.neverProtect: Org aliases or usernames to never confirm (escape hatch for a known throwaway scratch org). Wins over every other rule.
